biological-market.title: Biological Market
biological-market.info: Partners trade — carbon for phosphorus. Shift the exchange rate; each side accepts or defects until a temporary equilibrium holds.

carrying-capacity.title: Carrying Capacity
carrying-capacity.info: Logistic growth toward ceiling K. Drag K; the sigmoid reshapes. Toggle overshoot and the population boom-busts around the line.

competitive-exclusion-principle.title: Competitive Exclusion
competitive-exclusion-principle.info: Identical niches, one winner. Nudge relative fitness; only the knife-edge lets both persist — usually the fitter drives the other to zero.

density-dependence.title: Density Dependence
density-dependence.info: Per-capita growth falls as the crowd thickens. Add bodies; the growth gauge drops — crowding is the brake.

ecological-niche.title: Ecological Niche
ecological-niche.info: A hypervolume of tolerances. Slide axes — temperature, prey size, activity window — and the niche volume reshapes.

ecological-resilience.title: Ecological Resilience
ecological-resilience.info: Ball-in-basin. Perturb the system; a deep basin pulls it home, a shallow one lets it escape. Depth is resilience.

functional-response.title: Functional Response
functional-response.info: Predator intake vs prey density — Type I linear, II saturating, III sigmoid. Handling time bends Type II.

fundamental-niche.title: Fundamental Niche
fundamental-niche.info: Full potential range without enemies. Toggle competitors; the translucent zone shrinks toward the realized niche.

insurance-hypothesis.title: Insurance Hypothesis
insurance-hypothesis.info: Diversity buffers function. Fire stress on a diverse plot vs monoculture — redundancy holds the line; monoculture folds.

keystone-species.title: Keystone Species
keystone-species.info: Remove the keystone and the web cascades. Remove a peripheral node and almost nothing moves. Identity, not biomass, is power.

landscape-of-fear.title: Landscape of Fear
landscape-of-fear.info: Prey map risk, not just calories. Place predators; the foraging heatmap empties red zones even when food sits there.

life-dinner-principle.title: Life–Dinner Principle
life-dinner-principle.info: Prey runs for life; predator for a meal. Selection pressure bars show why prey often evolves the edge. Tilt the asymmetry.

lotka-volterra-equations.title: Lotka–Volterra
lotka-volterra-equations.info: Classic predator–prey ODEs. Tune birth, death, attack, conversion; the phase spiral and time series reshape live.

mutualism.title: Mutualism
mutualism.info: Reciprocal benefit. Sever the link and both fitness meters drop; restore it and the scale balances again.

niche-partitioning.title: Niche Partitioning
niche-partitioning.info: Share a resource axis by spreading use curves. Overlap spikes competition; partition and coexistence stabilizes.

optimal-foraging-theory.title: Optimal Foraging
optimal-foraging-theory.info: Patches differ in return and travel cost. Marginal-value theorem marks the optimal leave time as you set patch value.

paradox-of-enrichment.title: Paradox of Enrichment
paradox-of-enrichment.info: Add resources and the system can destabilize. Raise K; oscillations grow until crash — enrichment is not always mercy.

prey-switching.title: Prey Switching
prey-switching.info: As one prey thins, the predator shifts to the abundant type. Diet pie tracks frequency-dependent choice.

quorum-sensing.title: Quorum Sensing
quorum-sensing.info: Each cell whispers a signal. Cross the density threshold and the colony flips behavior together — add cells to tip it.

realized-niche.title: Realized Niche
realized-niche.info: Fundamental niche minus enemies. Toggle competitors and predators; the usable zone shrinks to what remains.

source-sink-dynamics.title: Source–Sink Dynamics
source-sink-dynamics.info: Source births exceed deaths; sink survives only on immigrants. Tune rates and watch the arrow keep the sink alive.

planetary-boundaries.title: Planetary Boundaries
planetary-boundaries.info: Nine wedges of Earth-system safe space. Push a boundary past its limit and it flares red — the operating envelope.

foundation-species.title: Foundation species
foundation-species.info: A keystone's importance is disproportionate to its bulk. Slide the biomass share and watch the same removal effect change category — extraordinary at low bulk, merely proportional at high.
foundation-species.axis: Rare  ←   biomass share   →  most of it
foundation-species.verdictFoundation: Most of the biomass. It is the habitat, not a keystone

ecosystem-engineer.title: Ecosystem engineer
ecosystem-engineer.info: Two ways to build a habitat. One organism moves material around; the other simply grows, and its own body becomes the structure.

verdict.allogenic: The beaver carries the material. The dam is not its body
verdict.autogenic: Nothing was carried. The organism is the structure

caption.autogenic: Habitat made of its own tissue

autogenic-engineer.title: Autogenic engineer
autogenic-engineer.info: Its own body is the change. Nothing is assembled and nothing is carried — the tissue accumulates, and the habitat appears with it.
autogenic-engineer.axis: Habitat accumulates as the body does

verdict.young: Living wood, and nobody's address yet
verdict.mature: Bark and limbs enough for a few tenants
verdict.old: The organism has become a habitat

keystone-structure.title: Keystone structure
keystone-structure.info: One tree in an empty field. Its footprint is trivial and the share of life routed through it is not — which is where the word 'keystone' does honest work.
keystone-structure.axis: A single feature in a cleared landscape
keystone-structure.verdictPresent: A waypoint, a seed focus, an island of habitat
keystone-structure.verdictGone: The crossings scatter and the seed rain has no focus

dominant-species.title: Dominant species
dominant-species.info: High biomass, two different jobs. A dominant monopolises the resource; a foundation has the same bulk and everything depends on its structure.
dominant-species.axis: Same biomass, different amount depended on

verdict.dominant: It takes the light. Almost nothing lives on it
verdict.foundation: The same bulk, and everything is rooted in it

canopy-soil.title: Canopy soil
canopy-soil.info: Soil that never touched the ground. Epiphyte debris accumulates on a limb, decade after decade, until it has its own fauna a hundred metres up.
canopy-soil.verdictBare: Bare bark. Nothing to live in yet
canopy-soil.verdictLiving: Genuine soil, with its own community, in the air

tree-hollow.title: Tree hollow
tree-hollow.info: A cavity is not excavated, it is waited for. Nothing happens for a century; then a small hole opens, and only much later one large enough for a substantial animal.
tree-hollow.axis: Fungi, insects and injury, working slowly

verdict.none: No cavity at any age below about a century
verdict.small: A small hollow — enough for an insect or a small bird
verdict.medium: Large enough for a bird or possum to breed in
verdict.large: Centuries of decay. No planting shortens this

co-extinction.title: Co-extinction
co-extinction.info: The shape of the loss depends on how fussy the dependent is. A strict obligate tracks its host one-to-one; a generalist hangs on until the whole host network gives way.

extinction-debt.title: Extinction debt
extinction-debt.info: The habitat goes at year zero; the extinctions are paid later, by instalment. Scrub forward and watch survivors drain away long after the machinery left.
extinction-debt.axis: Years after the habitat was destroyed  →
extinction-debt.verdictOwed: {n}% of the species present are already doomed
extinction-debt.verdictPaid: The debt is settled. This is the new equilibrium

functional-extinction.title: Functional extinction
functional-extinction.info: Alive as tissue, gone as a participant. The roots keep sending up shoots and the blight keeps killing each one before it can reproduce.
functional-extinction.axis: The same root system, a century apart

verdict.before: Mature, seeding, and doing its ecological job
verdict.after: Not extinct. Also no longer part of the forest

biological-legacy.title: Biological legacy
biological-legacy.info: What a catastrophe leaves behind is not debris — it is the template the next forest is built on. Tidy the site and recovery starts from far less.
biological-legacy.axis: The same burn, cleaned up or left alone

verdict.legacies: Snags, logs and roots: the next forest has a template
verdict.salvaged: The fire left the template. The cleanup removed it

nurse-log.title: Nurse log
nurse-log.info: A fallen giant's second career. Seedlings root along its length in a line, and a century later that line is still legible as a colonnade of mature trunks.
nurse-log.axis: One fallen trunk, read across a century
nurse-log.verdictLog: Wet, soft, and raised above the competition
nurse-log.verdictRooting: Seedlings rooting along its length, in a line
nurse-log.verdictColonnade: The log is gone. Its shape is still standing

alternative-stable-state.title: Alternative stable state
alternative-stable-state.info: A ball in a landscape of two basins. Push it hard enough and it drops into the second valley — and easing the pressure does not lift it back out.
alternative-stable-state.verdictHolding: Pushed, and still in the first basin
alternative-stable-state.verdictFlipped: Over the edge. Releasing the pressure changes nothing

cultural-keystone-species.title: Cultural keystone species
cultural-keystone-species.info: One species threaded through a whole culture. Remove it and the loss is not only material: the words, the crafts and the calendar lose what they attached to.
cultural-keystone-species.verdictPresent: Material life, language and ceremony all run through it
cultural-keystone-species.verdictGone: Not only a resource lost — the culture must restructure

succession-arrest.title: The Same Blow, Three Futures
succession-arrest.subtitle: Recovery is set by what survived, not how hard the land was hit

hint.sterilized: Deep pyroclastic burial pyrolyzes the soil and its seed bank. With almost nothing left to build from, the land barely greens across a century — this is primary succession, and it is slow.
hint.blast: A lateral blast flattens the forest but spares roots, seeds and burrowers under soil and snow. Those survivors reseed the site from within, closing a canopy in a few decades.
hint.ashfall: A thin, non-sterilizing ash drape leaves the living community mostly intact. Resprouting is almost immediate — secondary succession at its fastest.

aria.sterilized: Recovery curve barely rising above zero across 120 years
aria.blast: Recovery curve climbing to near-full cover within a few decades
aria.ashfall: Recovery curve rising steeply to full cover within a few years

verdict.sterilized: Arrested. The land must build soil from rock

inhibitor-stack.title: Why the Ground Says No
inhibitor-stack.subtitle: A seedling must clear every gate at once — relieving one barely helps

hint.clear: Every inhibitor relieved. Only now, with all gates open, does a pioneer stand a real chance of establishing.
hint.active: {n} inhibitors still active. A germinant must survive all of them at once, so the surviving fraction is their product — vanishingly small.

inhibitor-stack.aria: Compound seedling survival of {pct} percent across the active inhibitors

nitrogen.name: Nitrogen poverty
nitrogen.detail: Fresh tephra carries almost no usable nitrogen; non-fixers starve.

toxicity.name: Acid & metal toxicity
toxicity.detail: Leached acids free aluminium and manganese that poison root tips.

crust.name: Crust & hydrophoby
crust.detail: Rain-packed ash seals into a crust roots cannot pierce; water runs off.

thermal.name: Thermal extremes
thermal.detail: Unshaded ash swings tens of degrees a day, girdling stems at the surface.

erosion.name: Erosion resets
erosion.detail: Rills and mudflows strip young roots or bury them under fresh sediment.

verdict.clear: All gates open — a pioneer can finally hold
verdict.gated: {n} gates still closed; the product stays near zero

recovery-chronosequence.title: How Long Is 'Recovered'?
recovery-chronosequence.subtitle: Five real volcanic recoveries on one logarithmic clock

sthelens.note: Mount St. Helens (1980): a mosaic. Blast-zone survivors drove dense scrub within 30 years while the sterile pumice plain still lags.
sthelens.driver: Survivors under snow and soil reseeded the site from within

surtsey.note: Surtsey (1963): a new basalt island stalled in sparse forbs for two decades — until a gull colony began delivering nitrogen and the curve jumped.
surtsey.driver: A seabird colony after year 23 supplied the missing nitrogen

krakatau.note: Krakatau (1883): sterilized outright, yet wet equatorial climate and bird- and bat-borne seed closed a rainforest canopy within 50–70 years.
krakatau.driver: High rainfall and fast animal seed dispersal outpaced the sterility

paricutin.note: Parícutin (1943): bare cinder cones stay depauperate 80+ years on — coarse cinders hold little water and build soil painfully slowly.
paricutin.driver: Coarse cinders drain fast and seasonal drought stalls pioneers

laki.note: Laki (1783): a subarctic flood basalt still carries mostly moss after 240 years — cold, dense rock and fluorine weather and colonize glacially slowly.
laki.driver: Subarctic cold and slow basalt weathering stretch recovery to centuries
